blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Medical image super-resolution (SR) aims to recover image detail from low-resolution observations while
preserving anatomically meaningful structure. This is particularly challenging for contrast-enhanced vascular CT, where vessels are thin, highly branched, and span a wide range of diameters and curvatures: small peripheral branches may additionally exhibit weak contrast against surrounding tissue ( Lesage et al., 2009 ) . At high upsampling factors, much of this fine image detail is poorly determined by the observed low-resolution image, making the reconstruction inherently ambiguous ( Ledig et al., 2017 ) .
blocks.zh:
医疗图像超分辨率(SR)旨在从低分辨率观测中恢复图像细节,同时
保存解剖上有意义的结构。 这对增强对比的血管CT来说尤其具有挑战性,因为船只薄而分枝多,直径和曲面范围很广:小的外生枝可能与周围组织相比出现更弱的对比(Lesage等人,2009年)。 在高取样因素下,这些细微的图像细节大多被所观察到的低分辨率图像所不好地确定,使得重建本质上模糊不清(Ledig等,2017年).

blocks.en:
Recent deep SR has progressed from deterministic regression to generative
reconstruction, enabling sharper and more realistic image detail ( Zhang et al., 2018b ; Liang et al., 2021 ; Ledig et al., 2017 ; Saharia et al., 2023 ; Yue et al., 2023 ) . However, visual plausibility does not guarantee anatomical fidelity. Errors that are small in image space can be structurally significant: a short discontinuity may disconnect an otherwise continuous vessel tree, while a spurious connection may alter its branching structure. Such failures are not well characterized by conventional image-quality metrics. High SSIM, for example, can coexist with hallucinated anatomical structures in medical reconstruction ( Muckley et al., 2021 ) , and improved image-quality metrics do not necessarily translate to better downstream detection performance ( Li et al., 2021 ) .
Deep-learning-based CT reconstruction may also blur or remove small vessels despite producing
visually high-quality images ( Koetzier et al., 2023 ) .
For tubular structures in particular, voxel-wise overlap alone does not fully characterize topological correctness, motivating connectivity-aware measures such as clDice ( Shit et al., 2021 ) . A reconstructed CT image can therefore appear locally plausible while still containing broken, missing, or incorrectly connected vessels. These challenges motivate explicitly incorporating volumetric vascular structure into the reconstruction process, rather than relying on image appearance alone.

blocks.en:
To address these limitations, we propose VascuSR , an iterative
anatomy-aware diffusion framework for CT SR that targets both image fidelity
and vascular anatomical plausibility. Rather than relying only on individual
2D slices, VascuSR represents vascular anatomy explicitly in 3D. This
representation provides richer information about vascular topology while
separating vascular structure from CT intensity and organ texture, making
anatomical refinement a simpler learning task. We therefore use a conditional
3D rectified flow to refine the vascular representation. A lightweight
multi-scale anatomy controller then transforms the refined representation into
conditioning features for the diffusion decoder. At each round, the vascular representation is re-extracted and refined
from the latest SR volume to guide the next reconstruction, so that
the anatomical condition and SR output are updated in turn through
the feedback loop.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are threefold: • We introduce explicit 3D vascular representations as
anatomical guidance for slice-wise CT super-resolution.
Separating vascular refinement from image reconstruction
simplifies structural learning while retaining HR supervision
for image fidelity. • We develop an iterative refinement–conditioning mechanism that
combines a conditional 3D rectified-flow vascular refiner with a lightweight
multi-scale anatomy controller, allowing anatomical guidance
to adapt to each updated SR volume. • We evaluate VascuSR on two public vascular CT datasets across image quality, vascular overlap, and three-dimensional vascular structure. VascuSR reduces class-averaged component counts by over 20% on both datasets and class-averaged MCD by over 10% on MSD, while comparisons with direct joint optimization support the benefits of the decoupled design.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Super-Resolution and Generative Inverse Problems
blocks.zh: 2.1 超解析和基因反向问题

blocks.en:
Super-resolution can be formulated as an ill-posed inverse problem, where a
high-resolution signal must be recovered from a degraded low-resolution
observation ( Wang et al., 2021 ) . Because multiple HR solutions may be consistent with the same LR
input, successful reconstruction requires appropriate priors over the missing
fine-scale structure. Deterministic SR methods learn such priors implicitly from paired
training data through a direct LR-to-HR mapping, using convolutional
architectures such as SRCNN, EDSR, and RCAN ( Dong et al., 2014 ; Lim et al., 2017 ; Zhang et al., 2018b ) ,
or Transformer-based models such as SwinIR and HAT ( Liang et al., 2021 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) . These approaches achieve strong
distortion-oriented performance, but training with pixel-wise objectives can
produce overly smooth reconstructions.

blocks.en:
Generative methods instead model a distribution over plausible HR solutions.
Adversarial approaches such as SRGAN use perceptual and adversarial objectives
to recover sharper image detail ( Ledig et al., 2017 ) , while diffusion models
provide a probabilistic reconstruction framework through iterative denoising.
SR3 conditions the reverse diffusion process on the LR observation, whereas
ResShift constructs a residual-shifting trajectory between LR and HR
representations for more efficient sampling ( Saharia et al., 2023 ; Yue et al., 2023 ) . StableSR and DiffBIR further exploit
pretrained latent diffusion models as generative priors for image restoration ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Lin et al., 2024 ) . More broadly, this coarse-to-fine
inverse formulation is common across AI for Science, including medical imaging
and physical-system reconstruction, where generative priors are often combined
with domain-specific constraints to restrict the space of plausible solutions ( Chung et al., 2023a ; Huang et al., 2024 ; Yao et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en: 2.2 Anatomy- and Task-Aware Medical Super-Resolution
blocks.zh: 2.2 解剖学和任务软件

blocks.en:
Medical SR methods incorporate domain knowledge primarily through either
observation consistency or anatomy- and task-specific priors. One line of work enforces consistency between the reconstruction
and the LR input in the image or measurement domain. Chung et al. (2023b) reuse a score model trained for MR denoising for post-hoc
SR, alternating reverse-diffusion steps with image-level data-consistency
updates. GAN-CIRCLE regularizes bidirectional LR-HR mappings through cycle
consistency ( You et al., 2020 ) , CMISR iteratively corrects
re-reconstruction errors ( Li et al., 2024b ) , and DynamicDPS applies adaptive
diffusion posterior guidance to low-field MRI enhancement ( Kim et al., 2025 ) . Such constraints improve agreement with the observed image or measurement.
However, this agreement alone does not ensure faithful recovery of fine
anatomical structures that are poorly resolved in the input.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: 3.1 Problem Setup and Framework Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 问题设置和框架概述

blocks.en:
Given a low-resolution CT volume x x , our goal is to reconstruct
a high-resolution volume y ^ \widehat{y} that preserves both image
fidelity and vascular anatomical plausibility.
As illustrated in Figure 1 , VascuSR combines
a slice-wise diffusion SR backbone, a 3D vascular refiner, and
an anatomy controller.
The backbone reconstructs high-resolution CT images, the refiner improves 3D vascular structure, and the controller injects the refined anatomy into the diffusion decoder.
The backbone and controller are trained jointly with HR supervision,
while the refiner learns vascular correction separately in the 3D vascular representation space, decoupling structural refinement from CT intensity reconstruction.
During inference, the vascular representation extracted from the
current SR volume is refined and passed through the controller
to guide the next reconstruction, forming an iterative feedback loop in which the anatomical condition is updated after each SR pass.
Appendix B compares this decoupled formulation with directly optimizing image and anatomical objectives in the SR generator.

blocks.en: 4.4 Comparison with Super-Resolution Baselines
blocks.zh: 4.4 与超级决议基线的比较

blocks.en:
On the re-annotated MSD Task08 set, SwinIR achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM,
consistent with the emphasis of regression-based SR on pixel-level fidelity.
Nevertheless, VascuSR achieves the best LPIPS, which captures perceptual
similarity in texture and local structure, and leads all methods across the
Dice and clDice measures of anatomical fidelity. These results indicate that VascuSR focuses more on improving vascular
structure recovery in SR images while preserving the backbone’s
image reconstruction capability.
A detailed comparative analysis of VascuSR and ResShift+Dice/clDice across
local appearance, vascular topology, and other aspects is provided in
Appendix B .

are reported in Table 2 .

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Discussion
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和讨论

blocks.en:
We introduced VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework for
vascular CT super-resolution that decouples three-dimensional vascular
refinement from CT intensity reconstruction and connects them through
anatomical conditioning. Across MSD Task08 and HVM,
VascuSR improves Dice and clDice over the matched ResShift backbone while
maintaining comparable image-level reconstruction quality. Connectivity and
centerline analyses further show reduced fragmentation and closer agreement
with reference vessel geometry. Further comparisons with joint optimization of image reconstruction
and anatomical objectives support the benefits of our decoupled
design in local image fidelity, vascular structure, and training
efficiency. These findings support learning an
anatomical prior in vascular label space and transferring it to SR through
conditioning, while retaining HR-supervised reconstruction as the image
objective.

blocks.en: Appendix B Why Anatomical Conditioning Rather than Segmentation-Loss Fine-Tuning?
blocks.zh: 附录B 为什么解剖条件 而不是分裂 - 损失精细图解?

blocks.en:
VascuSR starts from two requirements for vascular CT super-resolution:
reconstruct CT images that are faithful to the
HR reference while preserving vascular anatomical plausibility. A diffusion reconstruction objective addresses the first
requirement, but spatially averaged image agreement alone does not ensure
that the reconstructed vasculature is anatomically plausible. A 3D vessel
representation is therefore a useful source of supervision: it captures
continuity and branching across slices and, with more fine-grained segmentation,
can also provide vessel categories. The design question is how to turn this
structural supervision into a learning signal, and which architecture should
carry it.

VascuSR起源于血管CT超分辨率的两个要求:
重建忠于
在保留血管解剖学合理性的同时参考HR. 传播重建目标涉及第一个
但仅凭空间平均图像协议并不能确保
从解剖学上来说, 重建后的活体是可信的。 3D型舰只
因此,代表性是一个有用的监督来源:它捕捉到
连续性和分枝 切片, 和,随着更多的精细分枝,
也可提供船舶类别。 设计问题是如何扭转这个
将结构监督转化为学习信号,哪些结构应当
拿着

blocks.en:
The most direct approach is to add Dice and soft-clDice to the SR objective
and fine-tune the image generator through a frozen segmenter. This approach
works: on MSD it improves Dice and clDice over ResShift (Table 1 ).
To explain why we use anatomical
conditioning rather than direct fine-tuning, we first compare the two training
strategies, then examine the limitations of this fine-tuning baseline and the
advantages of VascuSR in image fidelity in the vessel neighborhood, vascular structure, and training
cost.

然后通过冷冻分层器对图像生成器进行微调。 这种办法
工作:在MSD上,它比ResShift改进了Dice和ClDice(表1)。

transfers this learned anatomical prior to SR while retaining HR
reconstruction as the image objective
(Equation 12 ).
